name: ground_c
prompt:
Three images are attached. The first is a finished sheet of 12 ground textures for a top-down 2D city game, in a 4×3 grid; the second is its layout; the third shows the game's finished art. The two squares at the right of row 3, cells 11 and 12, are to be painted again; keep every other square exactly as it is.

What was wrong: the first attempt drew rust-brown drip streaks running down the square, which gives the ground a direction; the game lays it under roads at every angle, so nothing may run one way.

Cells 11 and 12: older bridge deck concrete seen straight down, the same mid grey as cells 9 and 10 beside them, a shade darker: a calm smooth painted base, and scattered at random small round pits, a few small round rust-brown stain spots no bigger than a hand, and tiny hairline cracks no longer than a hand curving every way. No streaks, drips, lines, joints or anything running in one direction. Both squares the same concrete, same colours and density, so they join without a seam.

Each repainted square is filled edge to edge, right into all four corners, and stops exactly where the old square's edges were: no border, frame, rim, bevel, outline, shadow or vignette. Outside the squares the background stays fully transparent. No text anywhere. Crisp hand-painted look matching the first image's other squares; no blur, no photographic noise.
